title: CDC insert event with a null before-image and a populated after-image
rationale: The before/after envelope with one side null is the single most common shape in change-data capture, and the realistic test that a top-level explicit null survives beside sibling nested objects. Also carries an epoch-millis long that must not be narrowed.
catchesBugClass: A top-level explicit null being dropped rather than preserved; epoch-millis longs narrowing to double or int; two sibling nested objects merging or cross-contaminating during prefix grouping.
cannotCatch: It says nothing about the delete case (before populated, after null) - symmetric in principle, but nothing guarantees symmetry. It also cannot catch the empty-object variant, which makes an insert indistinguishable from a delete.

predicted.detail: before reconstructs as an explicit null; source and after are scalar-only so both stay objects; the epoch-millis long is never routed through double.
